submissions.title: Alabama data center law takes effect Oct. 1: Here's what it means for your power bill
submissions.excerpt: targets facilities that use at least 150 megawatts of electricity
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Alabama SB 270 took effect Oct 1, 2026. It requires the Alabama PSC to ensure that electric contracts for data centers with loads of 150+ MW recover their full incremental grid cost from the operator rather than shifting it to other ratepayers, as a condition of contract approval. This is a statewide utility cost-allocation/large-load tariff rule, not tied to a single project, so no projectId is given — it is relevant context for any current or future Alabama Power / TVA-served AI campus above the 150 MW threshold. CAVEAT FOR REVIEWER: this sandbox's network egress to WebFetch/curl was blocked for essentially all external domains during this run (including the tracker API itself), so I could not directly open the enrolled bill text (alison.legislature.state.al.us/files/pdf/SearchableInstruments/2026RS/SB270-enr.pdf) or the WBRC article to confirm the excerpt is verbatim rather than a close paraphrase from secondary search summaries. Please verify the exact statutory wording and the 150 MW figure against the primary bill text before raising confidence above LOW.
